sources.title: Structured Pinduoduo interview source containing the RandomSet prompt
Writer RandomSet deterministic and randomized validation

claims.text: The preserved source asks for RandomSet set/remove/contains/randomGet operations described as O(1) without specifying language, duplicate insertion, missing deletion, empty randomGet, concurrency, or whether O(1) means deterministic worst-case versus expected/amortized behavior.

Java SE 21 documents constant-time basic HashMap operations when the hash function disperses elements properly and constant-time ArrayList positional access with amortized constant-time append; the candidate correctly avoids upgrading those conditions into an unconditional deterministic worst-case O(1) claim.
The exact candidate keeps a dense array plus value-to-index map and repairs the moved element mapping during swap-with-last deletion, preserving size equality and index.get(values.get(i))==i.

Writer and independent reviewer validations cover duplicate insertion, absent removal, middle/last deletion paths, contains, empty randomGet, random-member validity, a HashSet membership oracle and repeated internal bijection checks under seeded randomized operation sequences.

validation.command: extract the exact candidate Java block, compile it in an independent harness, and differentially validate deterministic plus 150000 seeded randomized operations against an independent HashSet oracle while checking the array-index bijection
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_candidate deterministic=swap-delete duplicate=rejected absent-remove=false empty=randomGet-throws randomized=150000 reads=37444 invariant-checks=1180 oracle=HashSet null-random=rejected
checks: exact candidate Java implementation compiles under Java 21 inside an independent harness
duplicate insertion, absent removal, contains, empty randomGet and constructor null-Random behavior follow the candidate contract/code
middle removal and later removal of the moved element preserve the dense-array/value-to-index-map bijection
150000 seeded randomized set/remove/contains/randomGet operations agree with an independent HashSet membership oracle
the reviewer repeatedly checks values.size()==index.size(), index.get(values.get(i))==i, no duplicate array members and exact oracle membership
randomGet never returns a removed or otherwise absent member and the fully drained set rejects randomGet

findings: The answer preserves the exact RandomSet source boundary and labels duplicate insertion, absent removal, empty randomGet, Java generics and the strict-worst-case interpretation as implementation/analysis contracts rather than source facts.
The dense ArrayList plus value-to-index HashMap invariant is explicit, and swap-with-last deletion updates the moved value mapping before removing the tail.

The exact candidate Java compiles under Java 21 and independently matches a HashSet membership oracle across deterministic cases and 150000 seeded randomized operations while the internal bijection is repeatedly checked.

The complexity wording avoids overclaiming: Java SE 21 documents constant-time basic HashMap operations when hashes disperse properly, while ArrayList positional access is constant time and append is amortized constant time; the candidate therefore distinguishes expected/amortized behavior from an unstated deterministic worst-case O(1) guarantee.
The answer covers duplicate members, missing deletion, empty random access, swap-delete of a middle element, space O(n), random-member validity and the non-thread-safe compound-state boundary.
The direct ArrayList middle-delete O(n) pitfall and the ghost-index bug when removing the last element are both explained as concrete failure modes.
No fabricated production experience, business metric or incident is claimed; the project section remains an explicit mapping/verification prompt.
